text:
tim: heads up — noticed a 15-20% p99 latency bump on mistral-7b after the kernel-selector change landed earlier today.
sara: saw that in dashboards too. looks correlated with sliding-window traffic (longer prefixes).
devin: any profiling traces? could be fallback to generic GEMM for certain sequence lengths / rope offsets.
tim: yes attaching quick flame summary (cut):
```
flame profile: mistral7b/generation
hotspots: 1) gemm_generic_kernel 42%
2) kv_read_tile 18%
3) rope_mul_scale 8%
(when seq_len>2048)
```
aisha: interesting — kernel chooser has a threshold that switched to generic for tiled kv shapes when window wrap occurs. kernel scoring penalizes 'unaligned' tiles.
michael: that's the merged change (PR #3214) that tried to avoid bad padding cost; probably accidentally penalizes seq wrap cases.
tim: also reproduced locally: when client uses sliding-window with max_position_embeddings=4096 but model was loaded with 2048 cap we hit weird mask patterns and the chooser can't match optimized kernels.
sara: so two things: max_pos mismatch + kernel score mismatch. both lead to falling back to generic path which is slower and thrashes KV cache reads.
devin: small repro snippet I used: 
```
inputs = make_sliding_window(prefix_len=3800, chunk=128)
server.request(model='mistral-7b', seq=inputs)
```
-> observe step latency spike at window boundary.
aisha: kernel-selector currently uses (tile_size, head_dim, seq_chunk) tuple. when rope offset wraps we set seq_chunk=0 for reuse and that triggers scoring hole.
michael: quick patch idea — treat wrapped windows as special-case and map to nearest compatible tile tuple instead of zeroing chunk. also add a soft penalty instead of hard exclude.
tim: I prototyped mapping to nearest tile and reran perf tests: p99 improved back ~12% but still 3% above baseline. leftover cost in rope scaling math and extra KV memcpy.
sara: what about prefetching the next KV tile for sliding window? that could amortize memcpy at wrap points.
devin: agree. we can queue a background prefetch for the next tile when remaining_prefix < chunk_size. cheap.
aisha: we also should add a small change to RoPE scaling: when max_position_embeddings != model_config.pos_emb, adjust per-head scaling factor to avoid per-token float mul churn. patch: compute scale_table once per batch and cache.
michael: can you paste the microbenchmark compare?
tim: microbench (local, 1xA10, batch=1, beam=1)
```
baseline: p50 17ms p99 54ms
post-kernel-fix: p50 16ms p99 47ms
+prefetch: p50 16ms p99 44ms
+rope-cache: p50 16ms p99 43ms
```
sara: nice. tests to add: 1) unit for kernel-chooser mapping logic, 2) e2e reproducer for sliding-window wrap that runs in CI perf.
devin: adding a lightweight replay test in perf harness should be fine — run it in smoke perf lane.
aisha: watch out for quantized kernels — mapping to nearest tile must ensure kernel supports same qformat (int8/4bit). otherwise fallback still required. add kernel metadata check.
michael: also flagged in infra: infra-bot: perf-regression alert created -> PERF-2026.
infra-bot: PERF-2026 created: mistral-7b p99 regression after kernel-selector change. linked traces and reproducer.
tim: plan of action: 1) revert hard exclude in chooser -> soft penalty mapping (PR queued) 2) prefetch next-kv tile heuristic (RFC + impl) 3) cache RoPE scale_table per-batch (hotfix) 4) add perf test + quant-kernel metadata gating.
sara: estimate: PR1 1 day, PR2 2 days, hotfix same day. can we ship hotfix first?
devin: yes hotfix is low-risk. I'll own PR1. tim will prototype prefetch.
aisha: I'll add quant-gating and extend kernel metadata schema.
michael: please include notes in release notes and mark Dedicated customers who hit high sliding-window traffic.
tim: pinging oncall to watch rollout tomorrow morning @sre. :eyes:
infra-bot: deploy job queued for branch/rope-cache-hotfix -> staging.
sara: thanks all — let's keep thread for post-deploy numbers.
